whatItDoes: Estimates capital gains tax for India, the US, the UK, Canada, and Australia. It computes your gain (sale price − purchase price − expenses), applies each country's holding-period rules, exemptions, and rates — including short-term vs long-term treatment, the Indian LTCG exemption, UK Annual Exempt Amount, Canadian 50% inclusion, and the Australian CGT discount.
whyItExists: Capital gains tax works completely differently across countries: some distinguish short- vs long-term, some apply flat rates, some use discounts or inclusion rates. A country-aware calculator applies the correct rules automatically instead of guessing a single rate.
whoShouldUse: Investors selling shares or crypto, homeowners selling property abroad or at home, expats planning cross-border sales, and anyone comparing how different countries would tax the same disposal.
useCases: Estimate tax before selling listed shares held long-term in India (₹1.25L exemption check)
Compare short-term vs long-term tax on a US stock sale, including NIIT
Work out UK CGT after the £3,000 annual exempt amount at basic or higher rates
See how Canada's 50% inclusion rate combines with your province's marginal rate
Check whether the Australian 50% discount applies after 12 months of holding
Plan whether to sell this year or next based on exemption resets and holding thresholds
instructions: Select your country — currency switches automatically but can be overridden
Choose the asset type: listed shares, unlisted shares, property, crypto, or other
Enter how long you held the asset where the country uses holding periods
Enter the purchase price, sale price, and eligible expenses
Add country-specific inputs when shown (filing status, taxable income, province, residency)
Read the gain, taxable amount, estimated tax, and per-item breakdown
examples: India: listed shares bought ₹100,000, sold ₹300,000 after 18 months → gain ₹200,000; ₹1.25L exempt; 12.5% on ₹75,000 → ₹9,375
US: $10,000 long-term gain with $40,000 taxable income → part taxed at 0%, remainder at 15%
UK: £20,000 gain with £30,000 income → £3,000 AEA applied; £7,700 at 18% + rest at 24%
Canada: $40,000 gain in Ontario → 50% inclusion adds $20,000 to income at combined marginal rates
Australia: $40,000 gain held 24 months by a resident → 50% discount halves the taxable gain
bestPractices: Include every eligible cost — brokerage, stamp duty, legal fees — they reduce the taxable gain
Check the exact acquisition date against the holding threshold before selling
For income-dependent systems (US, UK, CA, AU), enter realistic other income for an accurate marginal rate
Use the correct asset type — India taxes crypto at a flat 30% regardless of holding period
Treat results as estimates; confirm with a qualified tax professional
commonMistakes: Applying one universal 12-month rule everywhere — India uses 12/24 months by asset type and the UK/Canada use none at all
Forgetting that India's indexation benefit ended for transfers on or after 23 July 2024
Assuming crypto is treated like shares in India — VDAs are taxed at a flat 30% and losses cannot be offset
Ignoring NIIT (US) or Medicare levy (Australia) which add to the headline rate
Entering gross income instead of taxable income in systems that need your marginal band
faq: Is this tax advice? — No. It is an informational estimate for the selected tax year.
Which countries are supported? — India, United States, United Kingdom, Canada, and Australia.
Why does the UK not ask how long I held the asset? — The UK has no short/long-term distinction; the same rates apply however long you held it.
How is Canada different? — Half of any gain is added to your income and taxed at combined federal + provincial marginal rates.
What if I sold at a loss? — The calculator shows zero tax and notes the carry-forward rules for that country.
Are my numbers shared? — No, everything runs locally in your browser.
